To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IGF2 is expressed in a subset of breast cancers and is localized to the pericellular region of malignant epithelial cells.

IGF2 expressing stromal fibroblasts localize to the periphery surrounding malignant mammary epithelium, and that this localization is mediated by the interaction of the IGF2 ligand with the IGF1 receptor on the surface of the tumor cells.

IGF2 expression by fibroblasts surrounding breast cancer cells is regulated by paracrine signals, and that this growth factor is critical in the development and maintenance of the malignant phenotype.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IGF2 as a local growth factor in the genesis or progression of breast cancer.
elucidating the role of IGF2 as a paracrine/autocrine regulator of the malignant phenotype.
the paracrine/autocine regulation of breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IGFs and IGF-signaling molecules play important roles in the regulation of breast epithelial cell growth and that these molecules are potential targets for therapeutic interventions.
IGFs are involved in the genesis, maintenance, and progression of breast cancer, but the exact mechanisms by which they accomplish these tasks are not completely clear.
the IGF system is an important regulator of breast cancer growth and progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF signaling is a key component of paracrine/autocrine communication between stromal and malignant breast epithelial cells.
the expression of IGC2 by stroma surrounding breast cancer cells is a critical component of the local tumor microenvironment and is a key regulator of the growth of malignant breast epithel.
the IGF system is an important regulator of the growth and development and the malignant phenotype of breast epithelial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local environment of a tumor cell influences its phenotype and that the IGF system may play an integral role in the development of this phenotype.
the IGF2/IGF2R system is a key player in the regulation of breast epithelium, and that the IGFs may be involved in both normal and malignant growth.
IGF2 is an autocrine/paracrine growth factor that is important in breast cancer progression and that IGF2 expression is regulated by the tumor microenvironment.
